cards.name: VR Digital Glitch
cards.summary: Seam-aware digital glitch for 360 (equirectangular) footage: block displacement, RGB colour splitting and noise that wrap cleanly across the left/right seam. It also renders on flat footage, where it reads as a strong data-corruption glitch.
use_for: Short glitch burst on a cut between two news shots or a reveal
Corrupted 'breaking signal' feel on a hacked/fake-news segment in an explainer
Glitch transitions inside 360 / VR documentary footage without a visible seam
Trailer stingers: 2-6 frame glitch hits synced to bass drops
avoid: Leaving it on for whole shots: at default Master Amplitude 100 it destroys faces and on-screen text
Expecting it to animate by itself: without Evolution keyframes the glitch is a frozen pattern
Using it on a flat comp without checking the top/bottom edges: the frame is treated as a sphere, so glitch blocks near the edges can stretch differently than in the centre
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.name: Master Amplitude
params.does: Scales every other glitch setting at once (50 = all values halved, 0 = no effect)
params.typical: 0 at rest, 60-100 on the hit frames

params.name: Color Distortion
params.does: RGB split: slides the colour channels apart horizontally

params.name: Geometry Distortion X
params.does: Stretches/displaces pixels along X; works together with Distortion Rate

params.name: Geometry Distortion Y
params.does: Stretches/displaces pixels along Y

params.name: Distortion Complexity
params.does: Size of the glitch areas: low = big blocky chunks, high = fine small glitches

params.name: Distortion Rate
params.does: How much of the frame is covered by geometry distortion (0 = none, 100 = whole frame); NOT a speed control

params.name: Distortion Evolution
params.does: Phase of the distortion pattern (angle); keyframe it to make the glitch move

params.name: Color Evolution
params.does: Phase of the RGB split (angle); keyframe to make the colour fringes shift

params.name: POI Scale
params.does: Share of the frame affected around Point of Interest (100 = whole frame, 25 = a quarter)

params.name: Noise Strength
params.does: Opacity of a separate noise layer added on top of the distortion

params.name: Random Seed
params.does: Picks a different random glitch pattern with the same settings
params.typical: any 0-1000; change per shot so repeats don't match

cards.equivalent: VR Digital Glitch (Premiere, Immersive Video bin)
cards.scripting: Designed for 2:1 equirectangular 360 comps; on a flat 1920x1080 comp leave Auto VR Properties 0 and Frame Layout 1 (Monoscopic). Auto VR Properties = 1 reads layout/FOV from the comp's VR settings instead of the sliders. The glitch pattern is STATIC unless Distortion Evolution / Color Evolution / Noise Evolution (unbounded angle values) are keyframed, so a burst needs both an amplitude envelope and evolving phase (see recipe); a still Master Amplitude ramp alone just fades a frozen glitch in and out. Point of Interest ([x, y] px, default comp centre) is where the effect spreads from; POI Scale 100 = whole frame, lower values confine it around the POI; POI Aspect -100 = wider/shorter area, +100 = narrower/taller (per the Mettle SkyBox manual). Distortion Rate is coverage, not speed. Frame Layout labels come from the Immersive Video UI, not from the harvest. Animate Master Amplitude for bursts rather than toggling the effect. Needs GPU acceleration (verified 2026-10-13): a software-only (Mercury Software Only) aerender draws a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate instead of the image, a CUDA render draws the effect; set the project renderer to GPU (app.project.gpuAccelType, vfx.render_scenes(gpu=True), gallery.py --gpu) before building or rendering. The renderer a project is set to also becomes After Effects' default for new projects.

verified.note: GPU render: heavy data-corruption glitch over the whole frame: displaced blocks, RGB splitting and noise.
verified.recheck: 2026-10-13: re-rendered in live wave 1 (frames the old verdict was judged on: pve/work/gallery_pre_fix/)

cards.name: VR Fractal Noise
cards.summary: Generates cloudy fractal noise mapped onto a sphere, so it tiles seamlessly across the 360 seam and the poles, and blends it over the layer. On flat footage it gives a smoky, cloudy texture overlay.
use_for: Drifting fog/smoke overlay on a dark documentary establishing shot
Animated cloudy background plate behind titles or lower thirds
Seamless looping texture for 360 sky or atmosphere
Subtle texture layer (low opacity) to give flat graphics an organic feel
avoid: Default Opacity 100 with the default blend mode replaces the footage entirely with grey noise
High Contrast plus low Complexity looks like cheap 2000s screensaver smoke
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.name: Fractal Type
params.does: Noise style: 1 Basic, 2 Turbulent Sharp, 3 Max, 4 Strings
params.typical: 1 for soft smoke, 2 for sharper turbulent texture

params.name: Contrast
params.does: Contrast of the noise pattern

params.name: Brightness
params.does: Brightness offset of the noise

params.name: Complexity
params.does: Number of noise octaves (detail)

params.name: Scale
params.does: Size of the noise features

params.name: Evolution
params.does: Animates the noise shape over time

params.name: Opacity
params.does: Mix of the noise over the source
params.typical: 20-60 for overlays, 100 for a full background

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: How the noise composites over the layer (popup, 1-22; default 2 = Normal)
params.typical: 2 Normal with Opacity 20-60; 6 Screen or 7 Overlay over footage

cards.equivalent: VR Fractal Noise (Premiere, Immersive Video bin)
cards.scripting: For flat comps prefer the regular 'Fractal Noise' effect (more controls); use this one when you need seamless horizontal wrap or 360 output. cards.name: VR Glow
cards.summary: Adds a soft glow to the bright areas of the image (above a luma threshold), computed on the sphere so the glow wraps across the 360 seam. Optional tint colour.
use_for: Bloom on stage lights, rally lamps or sunlit windows in documentary b-roll
Dreamy flashback / memory look on an archival shot
Glowing neon titles in a 360 or flat motion piece
Tinted (golden) bloom for a warm patriotic sunrise shot
avoid: Low Luma Threshold plus high Glow Brightness blows out faces and white shirts
On flat footage the frame is treated as a sphere, so glow near the top and bottom edges can smear sideways and wrap across the left/right edges
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

cards.name: VR Plane to Sphere
cards.summary: Projects a flat 2D layer (title, logo, graphic, video) onto an equirectangular 360 frame so it looks undistorted in a VR headset; on a flat comp the layer is bent into a curved, pinched patch surrounded by transparency.
use_for: Place lower thirds, titles and logos correctly inside 360 documentary footage
Insert a flat news clip as a floating screen inside a 360 scene
Create a curved, bulging panel look for a stylised graphic (flat comp, creative use)
avoid: Using it as the final look on a normal 16:9 edit: the result is meant for a 2:1 360 comp and looks broken flat
Scale (Degrees) near 180 on text: extreme stretching at the edges
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.does: How many degrees of the sphere the layer covers

params.name: Feather

params.name: Projection Tilt (X axis)
params.does: Moves the patch up/down (degrees)

params.name: Projection Roll (Z axis)
params.does: Rotates the patch around the view axis

params.name: Source Roll (Z axis)
params.does: Rotates the source layer before projecting

params.name: Stereo Disparity (Degrees)
params.does: Depth offset for stereoscopic layouts

cards.name: VR Rotate Sphere
cards.summary: Rotates equirectangular 360 footage around the tilt, pan and roll axes, re-aiming the view or levelling the horizon. On a flat frame pan slides the image sideways with wrap-around, and tilt/roll bend it into curved distortions.
use_for: Level a tilted horizon in 360 drone or rally footage
Set which direction the viewer faces at the start of a 360 shot

Seamless horizontal scroll of a panorama background (pan only)
avoid: Tilt or Roll on flat 16:9 footage produces ugly bent geometry
Fast pan animation in a headset causes motion sickness

cards.name: VR Sphere To Plane
cards.summary: Extracts a flat, rectilinear (normal-looking) view from 360 equirectangular footage, like pointing a virtual camera into the sphere. On flat footage it shows a magnified, lens-warped crop of the frame.
use_for: Turn 360 rally or event footage into normal 16:9 shots for a news edit
Animate a virtual camera pan inside 360 footage for a documentary shot
Pull several angles from one 360 recording
avoid: Applying it to flat footage: the reframe is meaningless and softens the image
Expecting high detail: extracted views from 4K 360 footage are soft compared with native 1080p
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.name: Input Format
params.does: Projection of the incoming 360 frame (cube-map or equirectangular variants; popup 1-3, default 3)

params.name: Output Frame Width
params.does: Width in pixels of the extracted flat view (higher = sharper)

params.name: Output Frame Ratio
params.does: Aspect ratio of the extracted view (popup 1-5, default 5; one option is 'Unchanged')

params.name: Projection Tilt (X axis)
params.does: Aims the view up/down (degrees)

params.name: Projection Tilt (Y axis)
params.does: Aims the view left/right (pan, degrees) despite its harvested name

params.name: Projection Tilt (Z axis)
params.does: Rolls the view (degrees)

params.name: Invert Rotation
params.does: Checkbox: inverts the rotation direction

cards.scripting: Low confidence. Premiere has no sphere-to-flat extract effect (its VR Projection only re-projects/rotates 360 media), so this is AE-only. The harvested names for the Y and Z rotations both say 'Projection Tilt', so use the exact strings 'Projection Tilt (Y axis)' / 'Projection Tilt (Z axis)'. Input Format chooses the 360 PROJECTION of the source (cube-map vs equirectangular variants), not mono/stereo; 1 Cube-map, 2 Sphere-map, 3 Equirectangular (the default) (read from After Effects 26.0). Output Frame Ratio: 1 1:1, 2 4:3, 3 16:9, 4 16:10, 5 Unchanged (the default, keeps the comp/input ratio) (read from After Effects 26.0). There is no field-of-view slider: user reports say the view follows the comp's active 3D camera, so add a camera layer and change its zoom/focal length to widen or tighten the view (unverified; check a frame). Put the 360 clip in a comp of the desired output size and verify a frame before batch use. cards.name: Advanced Spill Suppressor
cards.summary: Removes green or blue colour spill (the tinted fringe and cast that a chroma screen throws onto a subject's edges, hair and skin) after keying. Use the Standard method (1) after the key: the Ultra method with Desaturate 100 greyed every hue on ordinary footage and on a green-screen plate alike (the subject too), whatever the Key Color, Tolerance and Spill Range.
use_for: Clean green fringe off an anchor or presenter after Keylight
Remove blue cast from hair and shoulders in a bluescreen interview
Neutralise green bounce on a talking-head shot filmed near a green wall
avoid: Ultra method with high Tolerance on real-world shots also kills genuine greens (flags, plants, uniforms)
Using it instead of a proper key: it only fixes colour, it does not create transparency

Ultra method with Desaturate 100: the whole frame turns black and white whatever the Key Color, Tolerance and Spill Range, on a green-screen plate too (measured live wave 3, the orange subject included) (a beige key at 80 / 90 and a blue key at 50 / 60 gave pixel-identical greyscale test renders)

params.name: Method
params.does: 1 Standard (auto-detects key colour) or 2 Ultra (uses the Ultra Settings)

params.name: Suppression
params.does: Overall amount of spill removed

params.name: Key Color
params.does: Screen colour to suppress (Ultra only)

params.name: Tolerance
params.does: How far from the key colour still counts as spill (Ultra)

params.name: Spill Range
params.does: Amount of spill colour range affected (Ultra)

params.name: Desaturate
params.does: How much spill pixels are desaturated vs colour-corrected (Ultra)

params.name: Spill Color Correction
params.does: How much the spill hue is shifted back to neutral (Ultra)

params.name: Luma Correction
params.does: Restores brightness lost when spill is removed (Ultra)

cards.scripting: Ultra Settings (Key Color, Tolerance, Desaturate, Spill Range, Spill Color Correction, Luma Correction) only take effect when Method = 2. Place it after the keyer in the effect stack. Key Color is '#RRGGBB'. Verified 2026-10-04: two Ultra demos with Desaturate 100 on test plate A (beige key #B4945C at Tolerance 80 / Spill Range 90, then blue key #0047BB at 50 / 60) both rendered the frame fully greyscale (R = G = B everywhere, stripes and faces included) and pixel-identical to each other, with no property warnings, so on footage without a screen the key colour and ranges did not limit the desaturation; a selective result at lower Desaturate is unverified. Live wave 3 on a synthetic green-screen plate: the Ultra demo (Desaturate 100, Key Color blue or the plate's #00B140) again greyed the whole frame, subject included, so the demo is now the Standard method (Suppression 100), the setting the green-screen recipes use after Keylight (not rendered alone yet). Status stays needs_input: it acts on spill after a key.

verified.note: On the green-screen plate the Ultra demo turned the whole frame grey, the orange-purple subject included, with the blue and with the plate's green Key Color: a global desaturate, not spill removal; demo changed to Method 1 (Standard), not rendered yet.

previous.why: the footage has no green or blue screen, so the spill removal it exists for was never tested; the card text was rewritten from this render
judged on the live wave 3 re-render on the second (synthetic) footage set, which has what the card acts on
previous.note: Still the whole frame in black and white (R = G = B in every region: stripes, faces, foreground blocks, palm), pixel-identical to the old render even though the key moved from beige at Tolerance 80 / Spill Range 90 to blue #0047BB at 50 / 60, so Key Color and ranges do not limit Desaturate 100 on this footage; status is now needs_input (needs green/blue-screen footage with spill).

cards.name: CC Simple Wire Removal
cards.summary: Paints out a thin straight line between two points (a wire, cable, boom pole, film scratch) by filling it with displaced neighbouring pixels, with pixels from another frame, or by making the band transparent so a clean plate on a lower layer shows through.
use_for: Remove a visible mic or power cable crossing a static interview shot
Erase a vertical scratch on restored archival film in a history documentary
Remove a power line from a locked-off drone or skyline shot
Hide a rig or support wire in a product or title shot
avoid: Curved or thick objects: it only handles a straight band, wider bands smear visibly
Moving wires without keyframing or tracking Point A / Point B

params.name: Point A
params.does: One end of the line to remove ([x, y] px)

params.name: Point B
params.does: Other end of the line ([x, y] px)

params.name: Removal Style
params.does: 1 Fade (band goes transparent, reveals the layer below), 2 Frame Offset (same position from another frame), 3 Displace (pulls surrounding pixels in), 4 Displace Horizontal (pulls only sideways)
params.typical: 3 for static textures; 2 when the wire moves over a static, locked-off background; 1 with a clean-plate layer underneath

params.name: Thickness
params.does: Width of the removal band

params.name: Slope
params.does: Edge softness of the band: low = gradual transition, high = hard edge

params.name: Mirror Blend
params.does: Pixel-replacement mix used by the two Displace styles

params.name: Frame Offset
params.does: How many frames ahead (+) or behind (-) to pull pixels from, Frame Offset style only

cards.scripting: Point A / Point B are layer-space pixels; for moving shots, keyframe them or link them with expressions to tracker points. Removal Style labels are from the CC documentation (default 3 = Displace). Fade only looks right with a clean plate on a layer below; on a single layer it punches a transparent line. Frame Offset only matters for the Frame Offset style and fails if the camera moves, because the background at that position changes between frames. There is no Premiere equivalent.

verified.note: At Thickness 60 the diagonal removal band (bottom-left flowers to top-right stripes) is now about twice as wide and plainly visible at gallery size: the stripes break into an offset seam and the centre detail and flowers smear along a clean diagonal edge, where the old Thickness 30 seam was barely noticeable.

cards.name: Color Difference Key
cards.summary: Older two-matte keyer: Partial B makes the key colour transparent, Partial A makes transparent the areas that lack a second, different colour, and the two are combined into the final alpha matte. Each matte has its own levels, giving fine control over semi-transparent areas such as smoke, glass or hair on blue or green screens.
use_for: Key smoke, glass or motion-blurred edges on well-lit blue screen footage
Second-opinion key when Keylight struggles with translucent areas
Pulling a matte from an evenly lit coloured backdrop for an explainer insert
avoid: Unevenly lit or compressed (H.264) greenscreen: noisy, chattering edges
Using it as the first choice: Keylight (1.2) is usually faster to a clean result
Low-saturation (near-white or grey) key colours: it keys almost nothing (a bluish-white #C8CDE2 key left the matching wall fully opaque in a test render)

params.name: Key Color
params.does: Screen colour to remove

params.name: View
params.does: Which matte stage is shown (popup, 1-10; default 8 = final output)

params.name: Color Matching Accuracy
params.does: 1 Faster or 2 More Accurate

params.name: Matte In Black
params.does: Raise to make more of the background fully transparent

params.name: Matte In White
params.does: Lower to make more of the foreground fully opaque

params.name: Matte Gamma
params.does: Bends the matte's semi-transparent midtones

params.name: Partial A In Black
params.does: Black point of partial matte A

params.name: Partial B In White
params.does: White point of partial matte B

cards.scripting: Keyed areas become transparent, so a demo render only shows the result over a contrasting layer or the comp background. Key Color is normally picked with an eyedropper in the UI; set it explicitly as '#RRGGBB' from a sampled screen pixel. The View popup has 10 entries (source, uncorrected/corrected partial A, B and matte, final output, and '[A, B, Matte] Corrected, Final' comparison views) (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Source, 2 Matte Partial A Uncorrected, 3 Matte Partial A Corrected, 4 Matte Partial B Uncorrected, 5 Matte Partial B Corrected, 6 Matte Uncorrected, 7 Matte Corrected, 8 Final Output (default), 9 a separator, 10 [A, B, Matte] Corrected, Final; render with 8. The 'Preview' header is a UI thumbnail and is not settable. Verified 2026-10-04 on test plate A (gallery frame = clip frame 42, a cool flash frame with a bluish-white wall; 85 of the clip's 99 frames have a tan wall, about #B0935E): a beige key #B4945C (Matte In Black 60 / In White 190) only made warm tones slightly transparent, and the wall colour #C8CDE2 (Matte In Black 100 / In White 200) left the wall fully opaque and only dimmed the navy areas and palm by about 10 levels, so this keyer needs a saturated key colour. The current demo is still weak; the likely fix, not yet rendered, is a saturated blue key such as #1A4FBF, which keyed the navy areas and a blue block in the Keylight and Linear Color Key demos on the same clip.

verified.note: The near-white wall key #C8CDE2 keys nothing of the wall; only the navy areas and palm leaves dim by about 10 levels (slightly transparent over black) while faces, foreground blocks and stripes are now untouched, so the frame reads as almost unchanged, a different but no stronger result than the old beige key that faintly darkened the warm tones.

cards.name: Color Range
cards.summary: Makes a range of colours transparent, defined by min/max limits on each channel in Lab, YUV or RGB space. Useful for unevenly lit or multi-coloured backdrops that a single-colour key cannot catch.
use_for: Key out an unevenly lit or multi-shade backdrop (e.g. a blue wall with shadows)
Drop out a coloured sky behind a building to place a new sky or graphic
Isolate or remove a brand colour from a graphic plate
avoid: Leaving min = max = 127 (the defaults): almost nothing is keyed

cards.scripting: The UI eyedroppers (Key Color / Add / Subtract) are not scriptable; set the six Min/Max channel limits (0-255) directly, ideally from pixel values sampled from the footage in the chosen Color Space. Keyed pixels become transparent, so check over a contrasting background. The 'Preview' header is a UI thumbnail, not settable. Verified 2026-10-04: the earlier demo box (RGB 165-200 / 135-170 / 75-115) matched almost no pixels of the gallery frame and only cut thin black outlines into faces, flowers and block edges. The demo box RGB 185-235 / 185-240 / 205-255, sampled from the bluish-white wall, keys about a third of the frame to black (the wall, the white stripes, block tops and bright highlights, with a few specks on skin) while faces, dark clothing, red stripes, block fronts and flowers stay; values are footage-specific, not a general preset (this clip flickers: 85 of its 99 frames have a tan wall, about #B0935E, that this box misses).

cards.name: Difference Matte
cards.summary: Makes pixels transparent where the layer matches a reference 'clean plate' layer (the same shot without the subject), leaving only what changed, such as a person who walked in.
use_for: Isolate a presenter from a locked-off shot when a clean plate of the empty set exists
Pull a rough matte of moving objects from static CCTV-style footage
Remove a static background behind a person for a cut-out explainer graphic
avoid: Any camera movement, light change or compression noise between plate and shot breaks the matte
Subjects wearing colours close to the background get holes

params.name: Difference Layer
params.does: The clean-plate layer to compare against (layer reference)
params.typical: a frame or clip of the empty background

params.name: Matching Tolerance
params.does: How different a pixel must be to stay opaque

params.name: Matching Softness
params.does: Softens the transition at the tolerance edge

params.name: Blur Before Difference
params.does: Blurs both images before comparing, reducing noise chatter

params.name: View
params.does: 1 Final Output, 2 Source Only, 3 Matte Only

params.name: If Layer Sizes Differ
params.does: 1 Center or 2 Stretch to Fit the difference layer

cards.scripting: Difference Layer is a layer-reference property (type 'layer'), which a spec cannot set: the script must set it to the clean-plate layer's index (e.g. prop.setValue(cleanPlateLayer.index)) and usually turn that layer's visibility off. The harvested default is 1; whether that is the layer itself or 'None' is not verified, so always set it explicitly. Shot and clean plate must be locked off and identically framed.
